newsitem.title: CHINA: SWIRE INDUSTRIES POSTS EARNINGS DOWNTURN.
newsitem.headline: SWIRE INDUSTRIES POSTS EARNINGS DOWNTURN.

text.p: Blue chip conglomerate Swire Pacific Ltd said the results of its industries division in the first half of 1997 were lower than the first half last year due to difficult trading conditions in some China operations.

"The industries division results were lower...due to weaker results from Swire Beverages' Coca Cola operations, and from the China operations of Crown Can Hong Kong and Carlsberg Brewery Hong Kong," the company said in a statement issued on Thursday.
Swire reported earnings of HK$3.32 billion for the six months ended June 30, 1997, an 8.5 percent increase over the year-earlier period.
The company did not give a profit breakdown by division.
Volume growth in Swire Beverages' Coca Cola in China was satisfactory but margins stayed under pressure, it said.
Other industries, ICI Swire Paints, Schneider Swire, and Tate & Lyle Swire all made satisfactory progress in development of their China operations, it said.

The company's trading division which includes car distributorships and continued to suffer from the difficult operating environment in the United States which depressed the division's results for the period, the statement said.
The motor vehicle business in Taiwn continued to be hit by unfavourable market conditions, it said.
In July 1997, the company became the exclusive distributor of Volvo cars in Hong Kong and South and central China, it said.
The results of the clothing, sporting goods and heathcare goods distribution units were in line with last year.
The marine services division reported "satisfactory growth" in profit, reflecting the improved market conditions within the offshore oil support sector," it said.
But the company said there was no growth in container throughput at Modern Terminals in first-half 1997. Subsidiary Hongkong United Dockyards Ltd also had a difficult first half, the statement said.
